targetTexts.1: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.
targetTexts.2: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
targetTexts.3: I have taken off my robe—must I put it back on? I have washed my feet—must I soil them again?
targetTexts.4: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.
targetTexts.5: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
targetTexts.6: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.
targetTexts.7: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.
targetTexts.8: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love.
targetTexts.9: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?
targetTexts.10: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
targetTexts.11: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
targetTexts.12: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.
targetTexts.13: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
targetTexts.14: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is polished ivory bedecked with sapphires.
targetTexts.15: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.
targetTexts.16: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
